title: Understanding the Pattern
text: The course IDs appear immediately after the word 'Data' and follow specific rules. They can be either three digits or $$\frac{one}{two}$$ digits followed by a letter from the set ['c', 's', 'x'].

title: Using Regular Expressions
text: In regular expressions, \d represents a digit. You can specify the number of digits by using curly braces, e.g., \d{3} for exactly three digits.

title: Optional Characters
text: To make a character optional in a regular expression, you can use the question mark '?'. For example, 'a?' matches zero or one occurrence of 'a'.

title: Constructing the Pattern
text: Combine the knowledge of digits and optional characters to form the pattern for course IDs. Remember, the IDs can be one or two digits followed by an optional letter from the set ['c', 's', 'x'].
